name: Conventional DLTS (100-420 K, 3 K/min) and Laplace-DLTS of the Z1/2 carbon-vacancy trap in 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes
plain_name: Find carbon-vacancy defects in silicon-carbide power diodes by scanning them from cold to hot
description: Ni/4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes on 25 um nitrogen-doped epilayers are scanned by conventional DLTS from 100 K to 420 K at 3 K/min (Vr -10 V, 1 ms pulses, 50 s-1 rate window); isothermal Laplace-DLTS near 325-330 K and 220-260 K then resolves the Z1 and Z2 components and their acceptor levels.
keywords: Find carbon-vacancy defects in silicon-carbide power diodes by scanning them from cold to hot

sources.citation: Acceptor levels of the carbon vacancy in 4H-SiC: combining Laplace deep level transient spectroscopy with density functional modeling (Capan et al., J. Appl. Phys. 124, 245701, 2018)

requirements.rationale: The DLTS temperature scan covered 100-420 K.
Optional: the published scan ramped at 3 K/min.
The diode is reverse biased and pulsed while its capacitance transient is recorded.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
